captions.hip-05-femoral-head-blood-supply: Illustration demonstrates the vascular anatomy of the proximal femur. The main blood supply to the femoral head is from the medial femoral circumflex artery, a branch of the profunda femoris artery.
captions.hip-06-proximal-femur-regions: Cinematic rendering of the proximal femur with the main regions of the proximal femur colored. The head and most of the neck (excluding the basicervical region) are intracapsular.
captions.hip-07-posterior-dislocation-radiograph: Posterior hip dislocation, with femoral head fracture and posterior acetabular wall fracture: Frontal radiograph of the pelvis shows a right posterior hip dislocation, with the femoral head displaced in the typical superior position. Note internal rotation of the femur, with obscuration of the lesser trochanter (yellow arrow). There is a posterior acetabular fracture (red arrow), partially obscured by the trauma board artifact. CT confirms a small posterior acetabular wall fracture (red arrow) and a small femoral head fracture in the region of the fovea (blue arrow).
captions.hip-08-dislocation-fractures-ct: Posterior hip dislocation, with femoral head fracture and posterior acetabular wall fracture: Frontal radiograph of the pelvis shows a right posterior hip dislocation, with the femoral head displaced in the typical superior position. Note internal rotation of the femur, with obscuration of the lesser trochanter (yellow arrow). There is a posterior acetabular fracture (red arrow), partially obscured by the trauma board artifact. CT confirms a small posterior acetabular wall fracture (red arrow) and a small femoral head fracture in the region of the fovea (blue arrow).
captions.hip-09-fracture-overview: No separate prose caption is provided; the source labels this figure 'Overview of proximal femur fractures.'
captions.hip-10-occult-fracture-radiograph-ct-cas: Occult fracture, evident on CT. Radiograph is negative. Coronal CT demonstrates a nondisplaced (stable) intertrochanteric fracture (arrow).
captions.hip-11-occult-fracture-ct: Occult fracture, evident on CT. Radiograph is negative. Coronal CT demonstrates a nondisplaced (stable) intertrochanteric fracture (arrow).
captions.hip-12-occult-fracture-radiograph-mri-ca: Occult fracture, evident on MRI (different patient from above). Radiograph is negative. MRI demonstrates a nondisplaced femoral neck fracture (arrows).
captions.hip-13-occult-fracture-mri: Occult fracture, evident on MRI (different patient from above). Radiograph is negative. MRI demonstrates a nondisplaced femoral neck fracture (arrows).
captions.hip-14-valgus-impacted-neck-fracture: Valgus impacted femoral neck fracture: Frontal radiograph shows a fracture of the femoral neck (arrows) with the distal part of the femur directed laterally, consistent with valgus. This fracture was treated with ORIF.
captions.hip-15-varus-displaced-neck-fracture: Varus displaced femoral neck fracture (different patient from above): Frontal radiograph shows a fracture of the femoral neck (arrows) with the distal part of the femur directed medially, consistent with varus. This fracture was treated with arthroplasty.

items.title: Acetabular cartilage and labrum
items.alt: Labeled diagram of the acetabular articular cartilage, labrum, pulvinar, transverse ligament, and ligamentum teres
items.see: The articular cartilage is horseshoe-shaped; the inferior gap is bridged by the transverse ligament rather than labrum.
items.why: It gives the spatial model for labral anatomy and the attachment of the ligamentum teres.

items.title: Normal hip radiographic landmarks
items.alt: Annotated frontal hip radiograph showing pelvic and proximal femoral landmarks
items.see: Trace the fovea capitis, femoral neck, trochanters, pubic rami, and intertrochanteric crest on one frontal image.
items.why: These landmarks anchor fracture localization and normal alignment.

items.title: Acetabular columns and walls
items.alt: Annotated pelvis radiograph showing iliopectineal and ilioischial lines and the acetabular walls
items.see: The iliopectineal line marks the anterior column; the ilioischial line marks the posterior column.
items.why: A break in either line can reveal an acetabular column fracture.

items.title: Axial hip musculature
items.alt: Annotated axial MRI through the hip showing muscles, neurovascular structures, and ligaments
items.see: Orient anterior flexors, lateral abductors, posterior gluteal muscles, and the medial obturator structures around the femoral head.
items.why: The cross-sectional map makes tendon, muscle, and neurovascular findings easier to localize.

items.title: Femoral head blood supply
items.alt: Diagram of the medial femoral circumflex arterial supply to the femoral head
items.see: The medial femoral circumflex artery courses along the femoral neck and supplies most of the femoral head.
items.why: Intracapsular fracture can disrupt this supply and increase avascular necrosis risk.

items.title: Proximal femur fracture regions
items.alt: Rendered proximal femur labeled with femoral neck, basicervical, intertrochanteric, and subtrochanteric regions
items.see: The femoral head and most of the neck are intracapsular; the basicervical region and more distal regions are extracapsular.
items.why: The location predicts vascular risk and guides clinically useful fracture description.

items.title: Posterior hip dislocation
items.alt: Frontal pelvis radiograph showing a posterior hip dislocation and associated fracture
items.see: The femoral head is displaced superiorly and the internally rotated femur makes the lesser trochanter less conspicuous.
items.why: The projection clues identify posterior dislocation even before cross-sectional confirmation.

items.title: Associated fractures on CT
items.alt: Axial CT showing posterior acetabular wall and femoral head fractures
items.see: CT shows a small posterior acetabular wall fracture and a femoral head fracture near the fovea.
items.why: Cross-sectional imaging defines fracture components that can be obscured on the trauma radiograph.

items.title: Proximal femur fracture overview
items.alt: Diagram showing femoral neck, basicervical, intertrochanteric, and subtrochanteric fracture lines
items.see: Compare the four clinically useful fracture zones and the valgus/varus distinction for femoral neck fractures.
items.why: This is the compact framework used by the following trauma examples.

items.title: Occult fracture: negative radiograph
items.alt: Frontal hip radiograph without a visible fracture in a patient with an occult intertrochanteric fracture
items.see: No definite fracture line is visible despite a true fracture shown on the paired CT.
items.why: A negative radiograph does not end the workup when clinical concern persists.

items.title: Occult intertrochanteric fracture on CT
items.alt: Coronal CT showing a nondisplaced intertrochanteric fracture
items.see: The paired CT reveals a subtle nondisplaced intertrochanteric fracture.
items.why: CT can disclose an occult fracture rapidly, although MRI remains more sensitive.

items.title: Occult femoral neck fracture: radiograph
items.alt: Frontal hip radiograph without a visible fracture in a patient with an occult femoral neck fracture
items.see: The radiograph appears negative even though the paired MRI contains a femoral neck fracture.
items.why: It reinforces the imaging mismatch that defines an occult hip fracture.

items.title: Occult femoral neck fracture on MRI
items.alt: Coronal T1-weighted MRI showing a nondisplaced femoral neck fracture
items.see: The low-signal fracture line is visible through the femoral neck despite the negative radiograph.
items.why: MRI is the reference standard when an occult hip fracture remains suspected.

items.title: Valgus-impacted femoral neck fracture
items.alt: Frontal radiograph showing a valgus-impacted femoral neck fracture
items.see: The distal femur is directed laterally relative to the head-neck fragment.
items.why: Valgus impaction is treated as a nondisplaced intracapsular fracture.

items.title: Varus-displaced femoral neck fracture
items.alt: Frontal radiograph showing a varus-displaced femoral neck fracture
items.see: The distal femur is directed medially, producing varus alignment.
items.why: Varus angulation is treated as a displaced intracapsular fracture.
